pointers.sentence: An add page and a change page differ in a few places, among them whether there is an object to load, which permission is asked, what the log says, and where the user goes afterwards; `ModelAdmin.add_view` and `ModelAdmin.change_view` each call `changeform_view`, the first with no object's key (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.add_view`).

For any method but `"GET"`, `"HEAD"`, `"OPTIONS"` and `"TRACE"` it runs `ModelAdmin._changeform_view` inside `atomic`, on the database the router gives for writing the model; the check stands outside the block (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.changeform_view`) ([Transactions: autocommit, `atomic` and savepoints](../connections/atomic.md)).
A `"POST"` carrying `"_saveasnew"` has its object's key dropped: from there on it is an add, of the data posted (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._changeform_view`).

A change loads the object with `ModelAdmin.get_object`, through `BaseModelAdmin.get_queryset`, and asks `BaseModelAdmin.has_view_or_change_permission`; only then, when there is no object, does it redirect to the index with a warning (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._get_obj_does_not_exist_redirect`).
Ship "abc" got the same, since `get_object` returns `None` for a key its field cannot convert (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_object`).

The view binds the form to the data, with the object as its instance, and `ModelAdmin._create_formsets` makes the inlines' formsets ([Inlines: `InlineModelAdmin` and its formsets](inlines.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._changeform_view`).

`ModelAdmin.save_form` calls `BaseModelForm.save` with `commit=False`: the instance with the cleaned values on it, unsaved (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.save_form`) ([Model forms: `ModelForm` and `fields_for_model`](../forms/model-forms.md)).
`ModelAdmin.save_related` calls the form's `save_m2m`, then `ModelAdmin.save_formset`, the formset's `save`, for each formset (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.save_related`).
An override of `save_model` must still save: the hook is for work around the save, says the documentation, not for a veto (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).
Validation checked the check constraint in a savepoint, since a transaction was open (`django/db/models/query_utils.py:Q.check`) ([Validating an instance](../instance/validation.md)).
The log's content type was cached by the change page's `"GET"`; else `log_change` selects it first (`django/contrib/contenttypes/models.py:ContentTypeManager.get_for_model`).

A `"GET"` of an add page takes the form's initial values from `ModelAdmin.get_changeform_initial_data`: every parameter of the query string, a many-to-many field's value split at its commas (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_changeform_initial_data`).

`ModelAdmin.render_change_form` adds the user's permissions and the options the buttons depend on, and returns a `TemplateResponse` of the template the model admin names, if any, or else of the first found of the model's, the application's and the admin's change form template ([The admin's templates and media](templates.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.render_change_form`).

Otherwise the response adds a success message linking the object's name to its change page, and redirects (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.response_add`, `django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.response_change`):

Both of these go to the change list, with its preserved filters, for a user who may view or change the model, and to the index otherwise (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._response_post_save`).

The buttons a page shows are decided by `submit_row`, which offered nora only "Save" and "Save and continue editing", as nora may not add ships (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_modify.py:submit_row`).

`ModelAdmin.save_as` puts a "Save as new" button on a change page, for a user who may add, in place of "Save and add another", and `ModelAdmin.save_on_top` repeats the buttons above the form (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_modify.py:submit_row`).

A copy that fails validation is shown with the change page's template and without "Save" and "Save and continue editing", lest the interface get confusing, says the comment (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._changeform_view`); with `save_as` true that leaves "Save as new".
The level may be a number or a level's name, `"warning"`; another name raises `ValueError` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.message_user`).
The default is `INFO`, which since 6.0 the admin styles apart from `SUCCESS`, the level the change form's success messages pass (`django/contrib/messages/constants.py`, `docs/releases/6.0.txt`).
